title: Percentage of Foreigners Working in Online Food Delivery Industry
what_it_is: Percentage of Foreigners Working in Online Food Delivery Industry

sections.label: Illegal foreign self-employed delivery riders
sections.summary: Foreigners cannot work as self-employed food delivery riders, and MOM has acted against social visit pass holders, with fines up to $20,000 or two years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, it is illegal for foreigners to work as self-employed delivery riders for food delivery applications, such as Deliveroo, Food Panda and Grab Food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has taken action against social visit pass holders working illegally as self-employed food delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, they can be fined a maximum of $20,000, or subjected to imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

sections.label: Two Malaysians caught delivering
sections.summary: In April this year, two Malaysians working for the food delivery business were caught.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In April this year, we caught two Malaysians who were working for the food delivery business.

sections.label: Penalties and abetting account use
sections.summary: Those caught face a $20,000 fine or two years' imprisonment, and Singaporeans who abet by letting them use their accounts face the same penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, those who are caught under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act will face a $20,000 fine, or an imprisonment of two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If the person is also abetting – as a Singaporean, allowing them to use your accounts – you can also be prosecuted and be fined a maximum of $20,000 as well as be subject to imprisonment of up to two years or both.
